summaryEn: Musk speaks to workers and customers at the grand opening of Tesla's Gigafactory Berlin-Brandenburg as the first German-built Model Y cars are handed over.
summaryZh: 在 Tesla 柏林-勃兰登堡超级工厂隆重开幕、首批德国制造的 Model Y 汽车交付之际，马斯克向工人和客户发表讲话。

segments.textEn: You know, and it's like it's very important to have reasons to be excited about the future because often people are depressed or sad about the future because they think it won't be good. segments.textZh: 你知道，而且，拥有一些能让人对未来感到兴奋的理由非常重要，因为人们常常会对未来感到沮丧或悲伤，因为他们认为未来不会好。但我们，我们在这里所做的是：我们每制造一辆车，每制造一块电池，都是在让未来变得更好。

segments.textEn: So what you're doing really matters. It makes a difference.
segments.textZh: 所以，你们所做的事情真的很重要。它能带来改变。

segments.textZh: 据他们所知，没有其他公司这样做过。而且就是，你知道，我们确实，在 Tesla 确实努力做正确的事，你知道，而且，你知道，我们希望成为一家你能够从内心和灵魂深处信任的公司。为了做到这一点，我们必须成为一家做正确之事的公司。

segments.textZh: 我也爱你们。

segments.textEn: Oh, yeah. Okay, so when is Tesla going to South America and maybe some other markets? Well, we definitely want to go to the world. The challenge we have right now, it's a high class problem, but the orders we have are well in excess of our production. So sometimes people will say, why aren't you in all these other markets? And why don't you make all these other different versions of the product, like different cars, like where's the Tesla semi truck and the Cybertruck and the Rosa and other things.
segments.textZh: 哦，是的。好的，那么 Tesla 什么时候会进入南美洲，或许还有其他一些市场？嗯，我们当然希望走向全世界。我们目前面临的挑战，这是一个高级问题，但我们收到的订单远远超过了我们的产量。所以有时人们会说，你们为什么没有进入所有这些其他市场？你们为什么不生产所有这些其他不同版本的产品，比如不同的汽车，比如 Tesla Semi 卡车、Cybertruck、Rosa 和其他产品在哪里。

segments.textEn: But the challenge we have, it's a good challenge, is that our orders far exceed our production. So, you know, a high class problem, but we need to have our production get to the point where it exceeds our current orders and then it makes sense to expand to additional markets and to have additional products. Because if we add complexity, but we don't add volume and we don't add production volume, then we've not actually done anything more because the good is a function of how many vehicles we're able to make.
segments.textZh: 但我们面临的挑战，这是一个好的挑战，就是我们的订单远远超过了产量。所以，你知道，这是一个高级问题，但我们需要让产量达到超过现有订单的程度，然后扩展到更多市场并推出更多产品才是合理的。因为如果我们增加了复杂性，却没有增加数量，也没有增加产量，那么我们实际上并没有多做成任何事，因为益处取决于我们能够制造多少辆汽车。

segments.textEn: So as we are able to ramp up production and satisfy demand in our existing markets, then we will expand to other markets and we will also add additional products. So, and I think last year there were a lot of supply chain challenges with chips. Everyone knows about the chip shortage. And then this year there's still some chip shortages. And then next year will be, I think, probably a challenge with total battery production.
segments.textZh: 所以，当我们能够提高产量并满足现有市场的需求时，我们就会拓展到其他市场，也会增加更多产品。所以，而且我认为去年芯片方面存在很多供应链挑战。大家都知道芯片短缺。而今年仍然存在一些芯片短缺。然后我认为，明年的挑战可能会是电池总产量。

segments.textEn: And then certainly if you start going like two, three years out, it's all about total how many gigawatt hours of battery are produced, that will be the limiting factor. And then going even further down into the supply chain, what is the rate at which battery materials are being mined and refined? And obviously we want to do that in an ethical and environmentally sensitive way. So that, that in the long grand scheme of things is, is how many terawatt hours of battery can be produced per year.
segments.textZh: 当然，如果你开始展望2、3年以后，那一切都取决于总共生产了多少吉瓦时的电池，这将是限制因素。然后再进一步深入供应链，电池材料的开采和精炼速度是多少？显然，我们希望以符合道德且对环境敏感的方式来做这件事。所以，从长远的大局来看，那就是每年能够生产多少太瓦时的电池。

segments.textEn: Our rough calculation is that it's about 300 terawatt hours is needed to transition the world to a sustainable energy economy. Like we're, you know, growing by, I don't know, 70, 80% a year on average and maybe even faster than that in the future. So, yeah, so that's, I think, the answer to why not more markets and why not more products?
segments.textZh: 我们的粗略计算是，要让世界转型为可持续能源经济，大约需要300太瓦时。基本上需要很多电池，所以我们想努力尽可能多地完成这件事。而且我认为我们其实做得相当不错。比如，我们，你知道，平均每年增长，我不知道，70%、80%，未来甚至可能比这更快。所以，是的，所以我认为，这就是为什么不进入更多市场以及为什么不推出更多产品的答案。

segments.textEn: So we're going to make it starting off with, well, not soon, but in a few months we'll make the special sort of deep dark red and sort of quicksilver. segments.textEn: Well, I don't think we're going to be using graphene, but we will use graphite. So there's plenty of that. You know, graphite is just carbon basically, so in a special form of carbon. But yeah, I think the batch of materials for long range, it'll be a nickel based cathode. The cathode is really the important part. They all have lithium and lithium is only like 2% of the cell. So nickel will be the one for long range, which is currently what we're using.
segments.textZh: 嗯，我认为我们不会使用石墨烯，但我们会使用石墨。所以石墨很充足。你知道，石墨基本上就是碳，是碳的一种特殊形态。但对，我认为用于长续航的那批材料会采用镍基阴极。阴极才是真正重要的部分。它们都含有锂，而锂只占电芯的约2%。所以长续航会采用镍，这正是我们目前使用的材料。

segments.textEn: And then for standard range of the iron phosphate and then for, and I think there's an interesting potential for manganese. And so the materials that are used for batteries at very large scale must be common materials. They're not common materials.
segments.textZh: 然后标准续航版本使用磷酸铁，然后对于，而且我认为锰有一种很有意思的潜力。而重要的是，比如你从非常大的规模来看，你必须说，好吧，我们需要数千万吨。最终可能会是数亿吨。所以，用于超大规模电池生产的材料必须是常见材料。它们不是常见材料。

segments.textEn: Can't scale.
segments.textZh: 无法扩大规模。

segments.textEn: Well, graphene. I know everyone loves graphene, but it's maybe we'll use it at some point, but graphene is a difficult thing to make.
segments.textZh: 嗯，石墨烯。我知道每个人都喜欢石墨烯，但也许我们会在某个时候使用它，不过石墨烯很难制造。

segments.textEn: But even graphene is made of carbon. So anyway, the fundamentals of scaling batteries are just say, like, how many millions of tons can be produced and produced in an ethical, environmentally good way. And I'm confident that we can scale to global volumes using iron phosphate and manganese cathode and then nickel cathode for long range. So.
segments.textZh: 但即使石墨烯也是由碳制成的。所以无论如何，扩大电池规模的基本问题就是说，比如，能生产多少百万吨，以及能否以合乎道德、对环境有益的方式生产。而且我有信心，我们可以利用磷酸铁和锰阴极来扩大到全球产量，然后为长续航使用镍阴极。所以。
